title: 色彩設計とアクセシビリティ
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: Editorial answers（編集・確認した解答）。元の本文・解説に基づき記述設問を英語4択へ変換しています。元記事の記述問題も引き続き利用できます。

passages.text:
Color wheels organize hues into a circular relation, but there is no single wheel that answers every design question. A painter mixing pigments, a screen combining light, and a printer controlling inks work with different materials and constraints. Even the word primary depends on the system: it identifies components chosen for a model or process, not three substances from which every possible color can be produced perfectly. A wheel is therefore a map for reasoning, and a useful map must state what territory it represents.

Designers often place hues opposite each other to create contrast or choose neighboring hues to build continuity. These are starting hypotheses, not automatic emotional commands. The same pair can change in appearance when its lightness, chroma, area, texture, illumination, and surrounding colors change. Simultaneous contrast shows this dependence: a patch may appear different against two backgrounds even when its measured stimulus is unchanged. Words such as harmonious or energetic also describe an interaction among a design, a task, a viewer, and a culture rather than a property stored inside one hue.

Digital interfaces make the distinction between color difference and readable contrast especially important. Two controls may have different hues yet similar relative luminance, so some users cannot distinguish them easily. Sufficient foreground-background contrast supports reading, but contrast ratios do not predict every aspect of perception or guarantee a good composition. Designers must also test text size, font weight, display conditions, glare, and interaction states. Measurement narrows uncertainty; it does not replace observation with actual users.

Color should not be the only carrier of essential information. If an error is marked only by red, or two lines on a graph differ only by hue, meaning may disappear for a viewer who cannot distinguish the colors, for a monochrome display, or for a poor projection. A label, symbol, line pattern, position, or written status creates a second route to the same information. This redundancy does not ban color. It lets color contribute to hierarchy and expression without making access depend on one perceptual channel. A responsible palette is not merely attractive; it states a purpose, survives changing conditions, and reveals how failure will be detected.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: One universal color wheel predicts the emotional response of every viewer.

options.label: B
options.text: Effective color design treats models as conditional tools and tests meaning, contrast, and access in context.

options.label: C
options.text: Contrast ratios make user observation unnecessary.

options.label: D
options.text: Accessible design should remove all color from visual communication.

questions.answer: The passage emphasizes purpose, context, and testing. 正解：B。色模型は条件付きの道具であり、意味・読みやすさ・利用しやすさを検証します。Aは普遍化、Cは利用者観察を省略、Dは『色だけに依存しない』を『色を禁止する』と誤読しています。

questions.prompt: Why does the author compare a color wheel to a map that must identify its territory?

options.label: A
options.text: A wheel is an exact copy of every possible color sensation in every observer.

options.label: B
options.text: A wheel eliminates differences among screens, pigments, and printing inks.

options.label: C
options.text: A wheel represents selected relationships for a specified medium, model, or purpose.

options.label: D
options.text: A wheel is useful only if it never states which mixing system it represents.

questions.answer: A useful model must state what it represents and where it applies. 正解：C。medium（媒体：画面・顔料・印刷物など）によって混色の仕組みが異なります。Aは模型を知覚そのものと同一視し、Bは材料差を消し、Dは明示が必要という本文と逆です。

questions.prompt: The phrase 'starting hypotheses' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to:

options.label: A
options.text: initial expectations that must be tested in context

options.label: B
options.text: universal laws that cannot be contradicted

options.label: C
options.text: decorative names with no practical use

options.label: D
options.text: final measurements of relative luminance

questions.answer: A hypothesis is a testable expectation, not a guaranteed result. 正解：A。hypothesis（仮説）は証拠によって確認・修正できる予想です。Bは不変の法則へ強め、Cは実用性を否定し、Dは出発点を最終測定値に置き換えています。

questions.prompt: Why does choosing opposite hues not guarantee strong readable contrast?

options.label: A
options.text: Opposite hues necessarily have identical measured stimuli under every condition.

options.label: B
options.text: Color wheels specify all the viewing conditions that affect readability.

options.label: C
options.text: Foreground-background contrast is irrelevant whenever the hues are different.

options.label: D
options.text: Relative luminance may be similar, and illumination or surrounding colors may alter appearance.

questions.answer: Hue difference alone does not capture every variable involved in reading. 正解：D。relative luminance（相対輝度）と周囲条件も必要です。Aは刺激が必ず同じという根拠のない主張、Bは模型の範囲を過大視、Cは前景と背景のコントラストを無視します。

questions.prompt: Why does the author regard contrast-ratio measurement as useful but insufficient to complete a design?

options.label: A
options.text: It measures all aspects of perception but says nothing about foreground and background.

options.label: B
options.text: It supports reading checks but cannot replace testing text, viewing conditions, interaction states, and actual users.

options.label: C
options.text: It has no relationship to readability and should be excluded from design work.

options.label: D
options.text: It guarantees a good composition whenever two controls have different hues.

questions.answer: Measurement reduces uncertainty without predicting every perceptual or practical outcome. 正解：B。contrast ratio（コントラスト比）は有用ですが、文字の大きさ・太さ・まぶしさ・操作状態も検査します。Aは適用範囲を逆転し、Cは有用性を否定、Dは構成の良さまで保証してしまいます。

questions.prompt: Which change best adds two non-color cues to an error shown only in red?

options.label: A
options.text: Use brighter red and a second shade of red, with no text or symbols.

options.label: B
options.text: Replace the red with blue and remove every other sign of the error.

options.label: C
options.text: Keep color if desired, but add a warning symbol and a written error message.

options.label: D
options.text: Hide the error whenever the display cannot reproduce the intended shade.

questions.answer: A symbol and a written message provide additional routes to the same meaning. 正解：C。redundancy（冗長性：同じ情報を複数の手掛かりで伝えること）が根拠です。A・Bは色の識別への依存が残り、Dは必要な情報自体を消します。

questions.prompt: Which revision of 'Blue creates calmness' best fits the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Under specified viewing conditions and tasks, a defined user group may rate this blue design as calmer than a comparison design.

options.label: B
options.text: Every blue hue makes every observer equally calm regardless of culture or task.

options.label: C
options.text: A measured blue stimulus stores calmness as a physical property that requires no observer.

options.label: D
options.text: Because context matters, no comparison of viewers' responses to blue designs can ever be tested.

questions.answer: Specify the stimulus, comparison, users, and conditions to make the claim testable. 正解：A。calmerは「より落ち着いた」。条件付きの評価へ改め、色だけが普遍的に感情を起こす断定を避けます。B・Cは本文と逆、Dは条件依存性を検証不能性と取り違えています。

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses 'Measurement narrows uncertainty; it does not replace observation with actual users'?

options.label: A
options.text: User testing makes every contrast measurement meaningless.

options.label: B
options.text: Measurements guarantee that all users will read the design correctly.

options.label: C
options.text: Uncertainty can be removed only by replacing users with numerical models.

options.label: D
options.text: Measurements help assess candidates, while observation checks whether real users can successfully use them.

questions.answer: Numerical assessment and user observation serve complementary roles. 正解：D。narrows uncertaintyは「不確実性を小さくする」。測定で候補を絞り、利用者観察で実際に意味が伝わるか確かめます。Aは測定を否定、Bは成功を保証、Cは利用者を置き換えています。

questions.prompt: Which plan best applies the passage to testing a university evacuation-route map?

options.label: A
options.text: Select colors people call attractive, and treat preference scores alone as proof that routes are clear.

options.label: B
options.text: Combine contrast checks with labels and line patterns, then test route-finding across viewers, formats, and lighting conditions.

options.label: C
options.text: Use hue alone for safe and blocked paths, and inspect only one ideal screen display.

options.label: D
options.text: Measure one contrast ratio and omit trials of route-finding speed and errors.

questions.answer: Test task performance and preserve meaning when color cues fail. 正解：B。route-finding（経路探索）の誤りや迷いを検査し、色以外の手掛かりも用意します。Aは好みと利用成功を混同し、Cは色と理想条件に依存、Dは実利用の検証を省いています。
